findings.title: verify() ignores session expiry
findings.description: verify() returns any session whose token matches without checking expires_at, so expired tokens remain valid forever. The docstring promises None when the lifetime has run out.

findings.title: require_admin() can never return True
findings.description: The condition uses `or` between two mutually exclusive `!=` checks, so it is always true and the function always returns False. No session, including an admin, can pass.

findings.title: revoke() raises KeyError on unknown token
findings.description: del self.sessions[token] crashes when the token is not present instead of being a no-op.

findings.title: bearer_token() crashes on missing/malformed header
findings.description: Splitting and indexing [1] raises IndexError for an empty or single-token header, which propagates to handle() and 500s the request.

findings.title: parse_lifetime() bare except hides bad input
findings.description: A bare except swallows any error (including non-value errors) and silently returns 0; it also accepts negatives without validation.

findings.title: peek() is not thread-safe and reports stale entries
findings.description: peek() reads self.entries without the lock and returns True for entries that have expired, contradicting the TTL semantics.

findings.title: set() evicts the wrong entry (not LRU)
findings.description: Eviction always picks list(self.entries.keys())[0] (insertion order) instead of the entry with the smallest `used` timestamp, so the least recently used entry is not evicted.

findings.title: warm() crashes when given a mapping
findings.description: Iterating `for code, target in pairs` assumes a sequence of pairs; a dict yields keys (strings), which then fail to unpack. The documented use is loading codes, likely from a dict.

findings.title: sweep() mutates the dict while iterating
findings.description: The loop iterates self.entries directly and deletes keys inside it, raising RuntimeError in Python.

findings.title: utilization() integer division truncates to 0
findings.description: `len(self.entries) // self.limit * 100` evaluates to 0 unless the cache is completely full (and divides by zero if limit is 0).

findings.title: flush() deadlocks acquiring the lock twice
findings.description: flush holds self.lock and then calls self.delete(), which also acquires self.lock (non-reentrant), deadlocking the process.

findings.title: LINKD_TIMEOUT_MS treated as seconds, not milliseconds
findings.description: ms is parsed but assigned directly to cfg.timeout, whose default is 10 (seconds). A 5000 ms setting becomes 5000 seconds.

findings.title: LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS treated as seconds, not milliseconds
findings.description: cfg.cache_ttl = int(ttl) stores the raw millisecond value into a seconds field, producing enormous TTLs.

findings.title: LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT is parsed but never applied
findings.description: parsed is computed and discarded; cfg.fetch_limit keeps its default of 32 regardless of the environment.

findings.title: cache_ttl/c size env parsing can crash startup on bad input
findings.description: int(ttl)/int(size) are not guarded; a non-numeric value raises ValueError during load_config instead of falling back to defaults.

findings.title: validate() always returns True
findings.description: Even when problems are collected, the function returns True, so callers cannot detect an invalid configuration.

findings.title: load_file() leaks an open file handle
findings.description: open(path).read() is never closed; on a long-lived service repeated reads leak descriptors.

findings.title: parse_report() mutable default accumulator
findings.description: rows=[] is evaluated once, so repeated calls append to the same list and return growing stale data.

findings.title: write_snapshot() leaks handle and skips close/flush
findings.description: The file handle is never closed and bytes are not flushed/fsynced before rename, weakening the durability guarantee claimed by the docstring.

findings.title: handle() crashes when Authorization header is missing
findings.description: bearer_token('') calls split and indexes [1], raising IndexError and 500ing the request instead of 401.

findings.title: delete_link() ignores ownership and session
findings.description: store.delete() is called with only the code; any authenticated user can delete another owner's link. The docstring requires the owner come from the authenticated session.

findings.title: admin_quotas() authorizes via a spoofable header
findings.description: Access is granted when request headers contain x-admin: true, bypassing authenticator.require_admin and the session role entirely.

findings.title: stats() divides by zero on empty store
findings.description: store.total_hits() / store.size() raises ZeroDivisionError when there are no links.

findings.title: report() name mismatch between write and read
findings.description: export_csv defaults an empty name to "links", but read_report uses the raw (possibly empty) name, so the read targets a different filename and fails.

findings.title: create() crashes on first link for any owner
findings.description: self.quota[owner] = self.quota[owner] + 1 reads self.quota[owner] before the owner exists, raising KeyError on every new owner's first link.

findings.title: create() mutable default tags list is shared
findings.description: tags=[] is evaluated once at function definition, so appended tags leak across calls.

findings.title: resolve() deletes live links and keeps expired ones (inverted expiry)
findings.description: The condition deletes the link when now < expires_at, so valid links are removed and expired links are counted and returned.

findings.title: rename() validates frm twice, never validates to
findings.description: validate_code is called twice on frm and never on to, so invalid target codes are accepted.

findings.title: page() off-by-one upper bound
findings.description: `end = len(all_links) + 1` asks for one entry beyond the list length (harmless due to slicing, but incorrect and confusing).

findings.title: success_rate() integer division loses fractional results
findings.description: `used // len(self.links) * 100` is 0 for any partial usage; the percentage is only ever 0 or 100.

findings.title: delete() does not decrement the owner quota
findings.description: The docstring says deleting gives the owner their quota slot back, but quota is never updated, so quota only grows.

findings.title: top() returns least-used links instead of most-used
findings.description: Sorting ascending and taking [:n] returns the lowest-hit links, opposite of the documented most-followed-first leaderboard.

findings.title: by_owner() uses substring match, not equality
findings.description: `owner in l.owner` matches any owner containing the substring, violating the documented exact-owner semantics.

findings.title: extend() revives expired links
findings.description: expires_at is always reset to now + ttl even when the link is already expired, contradicting the documented finality of expiry.

findings.title: quotas() returns the live internal dict
findings.description: Returning self.quota directly lets callers mutate store state, violating the snapshot contract.

findings.title: import_all() is not atomic and skips quota
findings.description: Links are inserted one by one with no rollback on failure and quota is not updated, contradicting the all-or-nothing contract.

findings.title: prune() mutates dict while iterating and returns wrong count
findings.description: Iterating self.links while deleting keys raises RuntimeError; returning len(self.links) reports survivors rather than removed count as documented.

findings.title: find_expired() returns a live generator over mutating dict
findings.description: The janitor iterates the generator while deleting links, causing RuntimeError. It should be a stable snapshot.

findings.title: warm_cache() returns before threads finish
findings.description: Threads are started but never joined, so the function returns immediately despite promising to wait for all probes.

findings.title: check_targets() raises IndexError when there are no problems
findings.description: Returning problems[0] with an empty list crashes; callers expect a safe value.

findings.title: count_for_owner() KeyError when owner has no links
findings.description: store.quotas()[owner] raises KeyError for an owner with zero links.

findings.title: Store has no synchronization despite being shared across threads and the janitor
findings.description: links and quota are mutated and iterated by request handlers and by the janitor thread without any lock. Concurrent create/resolve/delete/import/prune can race on the underlying dicts, leading to data corruption, lost updates, or a 'dictionary changed size during iteration' RuntimeError.

findings.title: prune mutates self.links while iterating it
findings.description: prune iterates 'for code in self.links' and deletes keys inside the loop. Any concurrent or even single-threaded use raises RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration.

findings.title: Janitor deletes from store.links while iterating a generator over the same dict
findings.description: loop does 'for code in store.find_expired(cutoff): del store.links[code]'. find_expired returns a generator that lazily walks store.links.items(); deleting on the first iteration changes the dict size and raises RuntimeError, so expired links are never reliably swept.

findings.title: Metrics counters are mutated and read without synchronization
findings.description: add_resolved/add_created and snapshot touch plain ints from multiple request threads and the reader in stats(). The read-modify-write is not atomic across interleavings, so counters can be lost; snapshot can observe a torn state.

findings.title: sweep mutates self.entries while iterating it
findings.description: sweep runs 'for code in self.entries' and deletes expired entries inside the loop, which raises RuntimeError on the janitor tick.

findings.title: flush deadlocks on its own non-reentrant lock
findings.description: flush acquires self.lock and then calls self.delete('__sentinel__'), which tries to acquire the same (non-RLock) threading.Lock again, so the admin flush endpoint blocks forever.

findings.title: Authenticator.sessions is mutated and iterated without synchronization
findings.description: issue, verify, and revoke touch the shared sessions dict from request threads with no lock. verify iterates sessions.values() while another thread mutates it, which can raise RuntimeError or expose inconsistent token state.

findings.title: peek, warm, stats, and utilization access shared state without the lock
findings.description: Only get/set/delete/sweep/flush are locked; peek reads entries unprotected, warm calls peek then set (TOCTOU and unprotected dict access), and stats/utilization read counters/sizing unlocked, racing with concurrent mutations.

findings.title: warm_cache starts worker threads and returns without waiting for them
findings.description: Threads are started and appended but never joined, so warm_cache returns before probes finish (violating its 'returns once every probe is done' contract) and any exceptions in workers are lost; callers and process exit can race the still-running threads.

findings.title: write_snapshot uses a fixed shared temp path, racing across callers/processes
findings.description: All callers and processes write to /tmp/linkd-snapshot.json and then rename it; concurrent snapshots overwrite or consume a half-rename of the same temp file, so the 'atomic snapshot' guarantee is lost.

findings.title: parse_report's mutable default argument is shared across all calls
findings.description: rows=[] is evaluated once, so every call appends into the same list, causing cross-request contamination and unbounded growth; concurrent callers see each other's rows.

findings.title: Janitor thread is neither a daemon nor joined on stop
findings.description: _running and _janitor are globals updated without synchronization and stop_janitor never joins the thread (or marks it daemon), so the process can hang on shutdown for up to the janitor interval and a second start_janitor would leak a thread.

findings.title: Expired links still resolve (expiry logic inverted)
findings.description: resolve() deletes a link only when time.time() < expires_at (i.e. while it is still valid) and returns the target for links whose expiry has passed. Expired short links therefore continue to redirect, defeating TTL/revocation and leaking targets past their intended lifetime.

findings.title: extend() revives expired links
findings.description: extend() unconditionally sets expires_at = now + ttl even for already-expired links, allowing a dead code to be brought back to life, contrary to the documented contract.

findings.title: Any authenticated user can delete any link (IDOR)
findings.description: delete_link() passes only the code to store.delete() and never checks that the link's owner matches the authenticated session. Any logged-in user who knows or guesses a code can remove another user's link, causing data loss.

findings.title: Owner is taken from the client payload, enabling impersonation/quota bypass
findings.description: create_link() uses payload['owner'] instead of the authenticated session's owner. A user can attribute links to another owner and exhaust or manipulate that owner's quota.

findings.title: Open redirect via unvalidated ?next= in /out
findings.description: The /out endpoint copies request['query']['next'] verbatim into the Location header without scheme/host allowlisting, enabling phishing via trusted-domain redirect.

findings.title: Admin endpoint gated on a client-supplied x-admin header
findings.description: /admin/quotas checks request['headers']['x-admin'] == 'true' instead of the session role, and auth.require_admin() is additionally broken (always returns False due to the impossible OR). Any authenticated user can set the header and read every owner's quotas.

findings.title: Path traversal in export_csv via user-controlled name
findings.description: name is concatenated into os.path.join(directory, name + '.csv') without sanitization, so '../' sequences escape export_dir and can create/overwrite arbitrary .csv files (also affected: read_report in export.py and /report in main.py).

findings.title: Session tokens minted with non-cryptographic RNG
findings.description: random.getrandbits() is predictable; an attacker who observes tokens can predict future session tokens and hijack accounts.

findings.title: Session expiry is never enforced
findings.description: verify() returns sessions without checking expires_at, so issued tokens live forever even though issue() sets a 12-hour lifetime.

findings.title: Hardcoded weak default secret
findings.description: When LINKD_SECRET is unset the service falls back to 'dev-secret-do-not-use', a publicly known value; any deployment missing the env var is trivially compromiseable.

findings.title: Constant-time comparison not actually constant-time
findings.description: secret_equals() uses ==, leaking the length/prefix of the expected secret via timing.

findings.title: Password hashing uses unsalted SHA-256
findings.description: hash_password() is a fast, unsalted digest, making stored hashes trivially brute-forced and rainbow-tabled.

findings.title: Permissive CORS with credentials enabled
findings.description: respond() sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, a dangerous combination for any credentialed cross-origin use.

findings.title: Token echoed back in 401 response
findings.description: The unauthorized response includes the presented token, which can leak tokens to logs or intermediaries.

findings.title: by_owner uses substring matching
findings.description: owner in l.owner treats owner as a substring, so 'bob' matches 'bobby', leaking another owner's links during filtering.
